design_caveat: chain design (adjacent tiers differ in one factor), not a full factorial; factors not independently randomized; all comparisons descriptive
key_findings: order pinning halves min-safe-action variation (68.3->34.1% SIFT, 63.2->30.8% Arxiv) at build-time ratio 0.80x/0.93x (no cost; slightly faster)
seed pinning under 8 threads is nearly inert (variation -1.3pp/-4.3pp) and the six D2 builds have six DISTINCT index hashes: parallel scheduling is a residual nondeterminism source
single-threading is necessary and sufficient for byte identity (D3 3/3 identical, variation 0) and carries the entire overhead: 4.73x/1.86x vs the pinned 8-thread tiers (3.52x/1.71x vs D0C)
a weaker order-only contract does NOT eliminate response variation - it halves it at zero cost
paper_impact: contract ablation table enters Section 7.3; D3 naming per definitions patch D7
the deterministic contract should be stated as requiring single-threaded (or deterministic-parallel) construction; 'fix thread count' alone is insufficient
order pinning is a free partial mitigation worth reporting for practitioners who cannot afford single-threaded builds
